key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the full processing–microstructure–property chain, where bonding, defects, porosity, grain size, and phase stability determine mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biological behavior.
engineering_relevance: Better control of sintering, sol–gel routes, and additive manufacturing can improve densification, geometry, composition, and reliability for structural and biomedical ceramic components.
method: Conventional sintering for densification and microstructure control
Sol–gel processing for composition and phase tailoring
Additive manufacturing for complex geometry and multimaterial fabrication
evidence_signal: This is a review article synthesizing prior studies rather than reporting a new experimental dataset or model evaluation.
watch_item: Brittle fracture and the porosity–strength trade-off remain major limitations, especially when scaling up or managing processing heterogeneity.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
